claims.claim: The NLI OpenLibrary search API base endpoint is https://api.nli.org.il/openlibrary/search and api_key is a mandatory GET query parameter.
claims.raw_snippet: Request format: https://api.nli.org.il/openlibrary/search?api_key={USER_KEY}&{search_string} . api_key: A personal key (mandatory) that the user receives after logging in to our API system. (Verified via Playwright past Cloudflare on the official NLI Search API docs page, 2026-06-04.)

claims.claim: Inside the query, multiple field,operator,value clauses are joined by ',AND;' or ',OR;'; the delimiter between the query and additional filters/commands is '&'. Operators include exact and contains.
claims.raw_snippet: The delimiter between the query and between [additional filters] parameters is "&" (logical AND). The delimiter inside the {query} string, between internal query conditions is ",AND;" (or ",OR";). Query string example: query=title,exact,jerusalem,AND;publisher,contains,jaffa,AND;language,exact,eng,AND;system_number,exact,990023677080205171,AND;start_date, contains,1925,AND;shelfmark,exact,Jer344 . (Verified via Playwright on the official Search API Common Usage page, 2026-06-04.)

claims.claim: Language and date filtering are query CLAUSES (language,exact,eng ; start_date/end_date,contains,YYYY) not standalone parameters. Date format is yyyyMMdd or yyyy.
claims.raw_snippet: A query compares a text to one / few / all descriptive attributes, and can filter by start_date / end_date and/or language and/or system_number and/or shelfmark. FAQ: Search for any item that contains the word 'Jerusalem' on title AND are written in English language AND has start_date/end_date between 19500101 and 19501231 -> query=title,exact,jerusalem,AND;creator,contains,Jerusalem,AND;language,exact,eng,AND;start_date,contains,1951 . (Verified via Playwright, 2026-06-04. Both yyyyMMdd '19500101' and yyyy '1951' forms appear.)

claims.claim: Valid material_type values are: books, journals, images, audio_video, scores, maps, archives, sheets, dissertations, manuscripts, media, databases, NEWSPAPER, Identity. audio/videos/articles/rareBooks are NOT valid.
claims.raw_snippet: Filters and Commands Valid Values: material_type -> books, journals, images, audio_video, scores, maps, archives, sheets, dissertations, manuscripts, media, databases, NEWSPAPER, Identity. FAQ: How do I search for Newspaper items on Jpress collection -> material_type=NEWSPAPER . (Verified via Playwright on the official user-help page, 2026-06-04.)

claims.claim: Valid availability_type values are: online_access, all_items, online_and_api_access, online_access_no_api, online_in_library_only, no_online_access.
claims.raw_snippet: availability_type -> online_access, all_items, online_and_api_access, online_access_no_api, online_in_library_only, no_online_access. (Verified via Playwright on the official user-help page, 2026-06-04.)

claims.claim: Pagination uses items_per_page (1-50) and result_page. There is no rows or start parameter.
claims.raw_snippet: items_per_page -> A digit in the range of [1-50]. result_page -> A digit (in the range of [count]/50). FAQ: How can I Paginate on results, when more than 50 items matches my criteria -> result_page=3 . (Verified via Playwright, 2026-06-04. No rows/start parameter is documented.)

claims.claim: sort_field (values title, creator, date_desc, date_asc) and output_format (json default, xml) are documented standalone commands; count_mode is true/false.
claims.raw_snippet: Commands: output_format, count_mode, result_page, items_per_page, sort_field. sort_field -> title, creator, date_desc, date_asc. output_format -> json, xml. count_mode -> true, false. Example: ...&output_format=xml&result_page=2&sort_field=title . (Verified via Playwright, 2026-06-04. Note the parameter name is sort_field with an underscore.)

claims.claim: Unknown / invalid non-mandatory parameters are silently ignored (request still returns results, unfiltered) with the skipped condition reported in an Errors response header.
claims.raw_snippet: Q: What if my query has syntax error - is it ignored, or will I get HTTP Error response? A: If the Search string has a syntax error in a non-mandatory attribute, the condition is ignored and an "Errors" Header will describe the error. Example: material_type=manuscripts111 -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK with Errors header code 1010 "...value : manuscripts111 hasn't been used because it is invalid". (Verified via Playwright, 2026-06-04.)

claims.claim: A guest user API key exists for trial access with limited query counts; full access requires signing up. The api2 docs cover api-key usage.
claims.raw_snippet: Guest user accounts have limited access permissions and can only perform a limited amount of queries. We recommend signing up to gain full access to our system.
